data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A panel of trained non-experts following a checklist is more reliable than a single expert for tasks where the primary failure mode is 'omission' (forgetting a step) rather than 'misinterpretation' (wrongly analyzing a step).","counterconditions":[{"case":"The task requires high-dimensional synthesis where checklist items are interdependent (non-linear).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The checklist is too coarse to capture critical edge cases.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The 'trained' non-experts lack the minimum threshold of domain literacy to execute the checklist items correctly.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The checklist acts as an externalized memory buffer that eliminates stochastic omissions, which are common even in experts (due to cognitive load or overconfidence), whereas the panel's collective training ensures a baseline of interpretation accuracy that approximates the expert's, but without the expert's vulnerability to single-point failure of attention.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
